defects.description: A name field's autocorrect and spellcheck switches are removed, leaving autocorrection and spellchecking on for a value a phone keyboard's dictionary does not know.
This field's autocomplete value is replaced with a token the HTML standard does not define, so autofill is certainly broken for it.
The new password is asked for a second time to confirm it, doubling the typing the new-password field already collects once.
A required house-number field is inserted ahead of the street-address field, splitting one address line into two and leaving an address with no number impossible to enter.
A required marketing-attribution question is inserted into the form, though creating the account uses none of its answers and the question could wait until afterward.
The form's primary button is relabelled with a bare generic word that says nothing about what pressing it does.
